title: A named worker-restitution schedule can exist without public proof that payment reached the worker
source_unit: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection Fair Workweek restitution settlements and proposed unclaimed-restitution fund
geography: New York City; Salz Management LLC and Theory LLC settlements

observations.period: March 2026 settlement announcement; scheduled payments from April 2026 through January 2027

denominator.unit: more than named workers across the Salz Management and Theory settlements

salz_restitution.unit: more than U.S. dollars required from Salz Management for restitution

theory_restitution.unit: more than U.S. dollars required from Theory for restitution

payment_route.value: scheduled checks or direct deposits through a notice administrator; workers may update address or bank information

worker_receipt.unit: missing mailed/deposited, returned, reissued, cashed, and individually received payment status

schedule_protection_and_recovery.unit: missing durable Fair Workweek compliance, household security, later work, trust, and exit

mechanism.value: A formal restitution schedule can shift payment-reachability and contact-update work to the worker without proving usable receipt or recovery

observations.method: Structured extraction from official NYC DCWP settlement and worker-payment pages; settlement obligations, payment timing, administrator contact, and missing recipient outcomes are kept separate.
observations.uncertainty: The public route does not publish worker-level eligibility, amounts, checks or deposits, returned payments, reissues, cashing, adequacy, household effects, later employment, trust, or exit. Institutional payment schedules are not recipient-side confirmation.
observations.subgroup: Fast-food and retail workers named or eligible under the Salz Management and Theory Fair Workweek settlements; no worker-level demographic, schedule, care, or payment outcome subgroup is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: A notice administrator and scheduled payment route may make restitution reachable for many workers, but a formal route can still fail through missing contact, delay, returned payment, or inadequate amount.

observations.period: July 9, 2026 proposed unclaimed-restitution fund; status checked September 19, 2026

denominator.unit: NYC DCWP proposed institutional fund route for unclaimed or unpaid restitution

trigger.value: respondent delinquency, insolvency, dissolution, bankruptcy, nonresponse, or other inability to satisfy restitution

claim_route.value: proposed discretionary and potentially partial disbursement after a consumer or worker claim

implementation.unit: missing adopted rule, fund balance, claim volume, eligibility decisions, disbursement, receipt, and adequacy

mechanism.value: An institution can recognize unclaimed-remedy failure and propose a public backstop without yet creating a reached remedy

observations.method: Structured extraction from the official NYC Rules proposed-rule page and DCWP notice of proposed rulemaking; proposal, claim discretion, and missing implementation are kept separate from actual payment.
observations.uncertainty: The rule was proposed rather than shown as adopted or funded in the checked route. No claim, disbursement, payment, recipient receipt, or durable recovery is observed.
observations.subgroup: Consumers and workers with outstanding restitution from eligible NYC DCWP enforcement matters; no eligible claimant population or distributional outcome is published.
observations.counterinterpretation: A proposed fund may become an important reachability mechanism, but proposed rulemaking cannot be counted as remedy receipt or full restitution.

related_sources.claim: NYC311 supplies the worker-payment contact and update route for eligible Fair Workweek restitution recipients.
DCWP's proposed notice describes the unclaimed-restitution fund and claim/disbursement framework.

boundary: This record establishes a current worker-restitution payment route and a proposed public response to unclaimed remedies. It does not establish worker receipt, adequacy, durable schedule protection, household recovery, trust, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the compact project event ledger derived from the official NYC DCWP and NYC Rules sources; worker identities, payment instruments, claims, and restricted files are not retained.
